study type: Secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial (TERMPROM trial)
exposure: prelabor rupture of membranes at term
time from prelabor rupture of membranes
early induction within the first 24 hours following term prelabor rupture of membranes
time after prelabor rupture of membranes
expectant management within the first 15 to 20 hours after prelabor rupture of membranes
outcome: Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit
Maternal infection (clinical chorioamnionitis or postpartum fever)
Prelabor rupture of membranes to delivery time
cohort: 4742 women with prelabor rupture of membranes at term (≥37+0/7 weeks' gestation)
finding: Immediate labor induction seems to be the optimal management strategy to minimize neonatal and maternal morbidity in the setting of prelabor rupture of membranes at term gestations.
mod_finding: Labor induction for prelabor rupture of membranes at term, compared to expectant management, did not affect the risk for cesarean delivery.
